analysis:
Documentation-only change in docs/architecture/inference.md. The changed ranges are head lines 3 and 810-813 and 829, and base lines 3, 810-811 and 827. The supplied units show base 2366-2597 (unchanged Flint/Bonsai/GLM text) and head 1-415. Within those units, only the date bump at head line 3 falls in a changed range.

The substantive change is visible in the patch excerpt. It documents that the GLM5Next video path now accepts variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks. Frames are indexed by i / nominalFrameRate in presentation order, as in the reference loader, instead of being refused with a 400. The remaining bounds are still documented: the decoded-frame cap maximumDecodedBytes (512 MiB, GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset), the 28,532 visual-token prepared-pixel cap, and the mediaReservation/videoTokenCeiling budget. Media requests are still excluded from prefix lookup and capture (CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint), so T-041 cache exposure is unchanged.

Accepting VFR inputs widens the media parsing surface for adversarial consumers (ADV-002) under TB-007. Availability concerns (T-029-style DoS) are also relevant: a VFR track with a skewed nominalFrameRate could change how many frames are decoded before the 2 FPS sample is complete. The documentation states decoding remains within the decoded-frame cap, and no source was supplied to verify that the cap and any decode-time bound hold for VFR timing. This is recorded as an unverified contract, not a finding.

The integration pass should check GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset and the VFR frame-indexing code for:
- frame-count and decode-time bounds when nominalFrameRate is zero, tiny or huge;
- an upper bound on the number of source frames;
- consistency of the media reservation.

The Nemotron Super text at head lines 1-415 is unchanged context. Its prefix cache is partitioned by authenticated tenant cache scope, and image requests are bound to a feature identity, consistent with T-041. No regression was identified in the supplied units.
